results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
**Mono-green storm for Premodern (brew, borrowing the mana and dork shell from Elves)**

**Plan.** Mono green has only two storm cards in Premodern: Sprouting Vines and Hunting Pack. So this is a mana-explosion deck. Elves, Rofellos and Wall of Roots make mana. Land Grant and Summer Bloom thin the deck and add land drops. Early Harvest, Llanowar Druid, Vitalize and Quirion Ranger untap lands or creatures for a second round of mana in the same turn. The mana goes into Hurricane for a lethal X to the face, with Hunting Pack as the backup. Cast with a large storm count, Hunting Pack makes a pile of 4/4 Beasts.

**Why the key cards** (card text checked in this session; the rest is my judgment):
- **Hurricane** hits each player, including you. Zuran Orb (sacrifice a land: gain 2 life) lets you go above your own X. I cut Zuran Orb from 3 to 2 and put the third in the sideboard. This is judgment, not measured.
- **Hunting Pack** costs seven mana, so it only works with a big mana turn. It is the fallback when a lethal Hurricane isn't there.
- **Vitalize** (G, untap all your creatures) is a cheap spell that adds storm count and doubles Rofellos and the Elves.
- **Rofellos** counts Forests only. Gaea's Cradle isn't a Forest, so it is a single-copy extra mana source.
- **Wall of Roots** is the one change to the deck. It makes mana without tapping and blocks Sligh and Goblins. I took it in main from the sideboard, in place of one Zuran Orb and one Vitalize.

**Mana.** The deck has 17 Forests and Gaea's Cradle, with perfect colour (100% on every turn through turn 6).
- Simulation with the Wall of Roots changes, over 5,000 games: 9% mulligans, 33.5% screw rate, 0.4% flood, and 2.93 lands in play on average by turn 4.
- The simulator counts only land drops and mana, not creature abilities. So its "payoff plus enabler castable by turn 4" figure (5%, up from 3.6% in the submitted list) understates the deck.
- I did not measure how often it actually kills on turn 4. Treat the deck as a turn 4–5 combo that is fragile to early removal.

**Matchups.** Shares are from the 30-day meta; my judgment, not simulated.
- **Enchantress (12.5%), Terrageddon (11.2%) and Standstill.** Good. They are slow and have little early interaction.
- **Sligh (9.9%) and Goblins.** Bad. Burn kills the dorks and Rofellos, and Sylvan Library costs life against them.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%).** Roughly even. It depends on whether the deck gets there before the Dreadnought does.
- **Hermit Druid (5.5%), UB Psychatog and Moneyball Black.** Bad. Hermit Druid is faster, and the others have counters and discard.

**Sideboard** (15 cards):
- **Against Enchantress, Replenish, Oath, Standstill and Stiflenought:** bring in Naturalize (4 copies now) and Crumble (2).
- **Against Enchantress and Hermit Druid:** bring in Xantid Swarm. It was in 265 Enchantress lists and 80 Hermit Druid lists. Its attack stops them casting spells for the turn.
- **Against Hermit Druid and Replenish:** bring in Tormod's Crypt.
- **Against Sligh and Goblins:** bring in Wall of Blossoms and the extra Wall of Roots, and cut Sylvan Library.
- **Against Terrageddon:** keep Zuran Orb. In Hurricane games, the third copy in the side is extra life gain.

**Unverified.** I assumed Stiflenought runs Phyrexian Dreadnought, so Crumble and Naturalize hit it. I didn't confirm the archetype list. The deck has no results history, because Hurricane, Early Harvest and Vitalize appear in no recent lists. The label is brew.

results.prompt: Give me a stock Goblins list for Premodern.
results.text:
This is the stock Premodern Goblins list: the most recent top-finishing Goblins list, a 5-0 at a Premodern League on 2026-10-14. I changed nothing.

**Plan:** Mono-red aggro. Goblin Lackey and Mogg Fanatic start the pressure. Goblin Warchief and Goblin Piledriver speed it up, and Goblin Matron and Goblin Ringleader keep the creatures coming. Siege-Gang Commander and Gempalm Incinerator finish games. Rishadan Port and Wasteland hurt opponents' mana.

**Key cards (judgment, from the list itself):**
- 4 Lackey, 4 Warchief and 4 Piledriver supply the early speed.
- 4 Matron and 4 Ringleader supply card flow. Matron also fetches the 1-of Goblin Sharpshooter, Goblin Tinkerer and Skirk Prospector.
- 4 Gempalm Incinerator and 4 Mogg Fanatic add reach and removal.
- 4 Port and 3 Wasteland sit among 24 lands, which also hold 17 Mountain.

**Mana:**
- The deck is 24 lands, with about 17.5 red sources. `check_deck` found no errors. Real Goblins lists average 23.97 lands and about 17 red sources, so this matches.
- In the simulation, 15.1% of hands were mulligans, 6.9% were mana screw and 3.7% were flood.
- Red mana was available in 97% of games on turns 1–2 and 91.7% on turn 3.
- By turn 3, 51.9% of games had a Lackey, Fanatic or Prospector in hand, or a Warchief or Piledriver. In 45.6% I could also cast one of them. The simulation only counts land drops and colors. It doesn't model card abilities.
- The utility lands cost some colored mana. That is the tradeoff for Port and Wasteland.

**Sideboard plan:** The metagame data covers the last 30 days. It lists Enchantress (12.5%), Terrageddon (11.2%), Stiflenought (10.4%) and Sligh (9.9%) as the largest decks. These plans are my judgment, not measured.
- **Sligh and other small-creature decks:** Bring in 3 Pyrokinesis and 2 Anarchy, and use Overload if they have artifacts. Cut some slower or clunkier cards, such as Goblin Goon or Gempalm Incinerator, if you need room.
- **Replenish, Hermit Druid Combo and other graveyard decks:** Bring in 3 Tormod's Crypt.
- **Stiflenought and other blue decks:** Bring in 3 Red Elemental Blast for counterspells and blue creatures.
- **Enchantress and Terrageddon:** Add Anarchy and Overload for their white enchantments and artifacts. Keep Wasteland and Port in. They are best when the opponent's mana is tight.

**Unverified:** I didn't check how this list performs against each matchup. The sideboard plans are judgment, not tool results.

results.prompt: Build a Replenish deck in Premodern that doesn't play blue.
results.text:
**Plan.** This is a white-black Replenish deck with no blue cards. Putrid Imp, Tireless Tribe, Zombie Infestation and Peace of Mind discard enchantments, and Enlightened Tutor finds them. Replenish (4 mana) then returns Opalescence, Worship, Pestilence and Parallax Wave together. Opalescence turns the other non-Aura enchantments into 4/4 creatures, so Worship stays active and Pestilence survives. Worship holds you at 1 life, and Pestilence ({B} per activation) then damages everyone, which you survive and the opponent doesn't.

**Review of the first list.** I made one revision, to the shell, mana and sideboard. The engine is unchanged.
- **Weak slots:** the 2 Peace of Mind in the main were weak. They only help against Sligh and Goblins, which are 9.9% and 4.4% of recent lists. They do nothing against Enchantress, Terrageddon or Hermit Druid.
- **Change:** I cut one Peace of Mind for a second Seal of Cleansing. The Seal answers Aura of Silence, Standstill, artifacts and Solitary Confinement. It also works as extra Replenish fodder.
- **Sideboard:** the second Peace of Mind moved there, and one Seal moved to the main.
- **Mana:** I went from 10 Plains and 10 Swamp to 11 Plains and 9 Swamp, with 4 Caves of Koilos. White needs more mana: Replenish, Tutor, Swords and Swords-type interaction, plus WW for Opalescence and Wave. Black needs BB only for Pestilence.

**Mana (simulated, 5,000 games).**
- The deck has 24 lands, which I kept because it needs 4 mana for Replenish. About 70% of games hit all four land drops by turn 4.
- Coloured mana is available in 55.8% of games on turn 1, 89.0% on turn 2, 91.5% on turn 3 and 82.2% on turn 4.
- The mulligan rate is 15.1%. Screw is 6.9% and flood is 3.7%.
- By turn 4, Replenish, a discard outlet and a Tutor are all in hand in only 18.1% of games, and castable in 9.4%. That is a strict test, since the deck can win through other routes. It still shows this is not a reliable turn-4 deck.
- Moving from 10/10 to 11/9 changed these numbers by 0.2 points or less. I chose it because of the colour needs above, which is judgment and not something measured.

**Matchups.** Meta shares come from the 30-day tool result. Everything about how a matchup plays out is my judgment and was not simulated.

| Matchup (share) | Assessment | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Enchantress (12.5%) | Hardest | They run Aura of Silence, Seal of Cleansing, Parallax Wave and Replenish, and their sideboard has Tormod's Crypt. Solitary Confinement stops Pestilence damage to them. Argothian Enchantress has shroud, so Swords can't hit it. |
| Terrageddon (11.2%) | Mixed | They run Disenchant and Aura of Silence, and Wasteland can hit Caves of Koilos. Replenish costs only 4 mana, so land destruction hurts less. |
| Sligh (9.9%) | Favourable | Worship plus Pestilence is strong. |
| Stiflenought (10.4%) | Unclear | Swords answers its creatures, but Wrath-type effects clear the creature that Worship needs. |
| Hermit Druid (5.5%) | Risky | It is fast, and Duress and Therapy are the only disruption. |

**Sideboard plans.**
- **Against Sligh and Goblins:** bring in 3 Circle of Protection: Red, 1 Peace of Mind, and the 2 Exalted Angels. Take out Duress, Tireless Tribe, and Zombie Infestation or Putrid Imp as needed.
- **Against Hermit Druid, Psychatog and Moneyball Black:** bring in 2 Cabal Therapy and 2 Tormod's Crypt. Take out Swords, and Tribe if needed.
- **Against Enchantress and Terrageddon:** bring in 2 Disenchant, the third Seal and 2 Cabal Therapy. Take out Peace of Mind and some Swords. Swords is poor against shroud Enchantresses.
- **Against Stiflenought and creature decks:** the 2 Wrath of God are an option, but they conflict with Worship. Use them only if you can win without a creature in play.

**Label: brew.** The Replenish package (Replenish, Opalescence, Parallax Wave, Seal of Cleansing, Swords to Plowshares) is borrowed from the 106 recent blue-white Replenish lists. Those lists run Intuition, Frantic Search and Attunement, which are all blue. The black discard outlets, Pestilence and Worship are my own substitutes.

**Unverified.**
- Matchup outcomes were not simulated.
- I did not test the Replenish turn-by-turn without blue card selection. The deck draws into its enchantments more slowly than the blue versions.
- Enlightened Tutor puts the card on top of your library, so you must draw it before you can discard it.
- I left Ancient Tomb out because of its colourless mana and 2 damage. This is a judgment, not a tested choice.

intent.goal: Deliver a Premodern Replenish-style deck (reanimating enchantments/creatures from the graveyard en masse) that uses no blue cards.

engine.thesis: White-black Replenish: cheap discard outlets and Enlightened Tutor put Opalescence, Worship, Pestilence and Parallax Wave into the graveyard, then Replenish returns them all at once. Black replaces blue's card selection and gives the deck Pestilence, which Opalescence turns into a creature that survives its own sweep. Premodern is a fast field (Sligh, Terrageddon and Stiflenought are each 10-11% of recent lists), so the deck leans on one-mana tutors and discard outlets instead of slower setup.

Worship holds you at 1 life, so Pestilence ({B} per activation) damages everyone and wins. Parallax Wave exiles blockers or attackers, and the 4/4 enchantment-creatures can attack.

Terrageddon and Armageddon decks (Replenish costs only 4 mana)
Slow control decks without enchantment removal

results.prompt: Build a Modern deck around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
Tainted Pact isn't legal in Modern, so I couldn't build around the pair as asked. Thassa's Oracle is legal. Demonic Consultation and Doomsday, the usual Pact-style piles, are also illegal. This is a brew with no tournament data behind it, built from the Modern Mill list's mana base.

**The plan.** The usual Oracle win needs a tiny library, and nothing legal in Modern shrinks yours fast. So the deck mills itself. Hedron Crab, Glimpse the Unthinkable (10 cards), Thought Scour, Wall of Lost Thoughts and Traumatize (half your library) all target you. The fetchlands thin the deck and set off Crab's landfall trigger twice each. Once the library is nearly empty you win with Thassa's Oracle, or with Laboratory Maniac or Jace, Wielder of Mysteries by drawing from an empty library. Thought Scour, Preordain and Consider can supply that last draw.

**Why these cards**
- **Spoils of the Vault** stands in for Tainted Pact. It tutors a named card, exiles everything above it and costs 1 life per card exiled. Naming a card that isn't in your library exiles the whole thing, so at 15 or fewer cards left it sets up an Oracle win.
- **Oracle** counts devotion to blue, so Crab, Wall, Maniac and Jace all lower the library size it needs.
- **Shelldock Isle** lets you cast a hidden finisher for free once a library is at 20 cards or fewer. I read its text for this, but I didn't test it.
- **Counterspell, Thoughtseize and Fatal Push** are light protection.

**Mana (22 lands, simulated over 5,000 games).** Mulligan rate was 19.3% (the Mill list sims at 20.4%). Land-screw was 10.5% and flood 2%. A coloured-mana check passed in 76% of games on turn 1, 86% by turn 2 and 94% by turn 5. At least one finisher plus one mill piece were castable by turn 5 in 67.2% of games. Both are blue-heavy; black is only a light splash (Glimpse, Spoils, Thoughtseize, Push).

**Honest odds.** On the play you hold about 49 cards in library on turn 5, and the deck needs to get that down to about 3–6 (my estimate; I didn't simulate the full kill). Draw odds, by turn 6:
- A finisher: 85.3%.
- A mill piece: 91.3%.
- Spoils: 49.5%.

I expect a typical kill on turn 6–8, which is slow against the top decks in the field (Broodscale Combo 14.4%, Prowess 9.9%, Energy 6.1%). That is a judgment, not a measured result. Expect a below-average win rate.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Against Prowess and aggro:** Spell Pierce ×2, Fatal Push ×2, and Wall of Lost Thoughts as a blocker.
- **Against Broodscale, Blink, Affinity and Eldrazi Tron:** Consign to Memory ×3, which counters triggered abilities and colourless spells.
- **Against Goryo's Vengeance, Living End and Persist:** Surgical Extraction ×2. Your self-mill feeds their graveyards, so also consider holding Glimpse back.
- **Against control and combo:** Force of Negation ×2, Mystical Dispute ×2 and Drown in the Loch ×2.

**Unverified:** the average turn the combo actually goes off, and how often Spoils can afford its life cost after fetchlands and shocklands. The simulator only models land drops and colours, not card abilities.

results.prompt: I want a Modern Merfolk deck that can beat the current top decks.
results.text:
**Deck: Mono-Blue Merfolk, stock.** It is the most recent top-finishing Merfolk list in the results: a 5-0 Modern League run dated 2026-10-13. I changed nothing. The results show 14 Merfolk lists, so the sample is small.

**Plan.** Land Merfolk early, often off Aether Vial, and buff them with Lord of Atlantis and Master of the Pearl Trident. Then use cheap tempo and counters to stay ahead. Harbinger of the Seas, Snapback, Sink into Stupor and Flare of Denial (sacrifice a nontoken blue creature to counter a spell) let you bounce or counter whatever the opponent does while you keep attacking.

**Key cards** (all text is from card lookups):
- **Svyelun of Sea and Sky:** it draws a card when it attacks. It gives your other Merfolk ward {1}, which makes your lords harder to remove. It is indestructible while you control two other Merfolk.
- **Sink into Stupor:** it bounces a spell or a nonland permanent. It also works as a land (Soporific Springs), so it counts toward your land total.
- **Snapback:** it can be cast for free by exiling a blue card from your hand.
- **Mutavault and Otawara:** the deck needs both a few manlands and some utility lands.
- **Cavern of Souls:** it helps your creatures resolve.

**Mana.** The deck runs 16 true lands plus 4 Sink into Stupor that can be played as lands. `check_deck` counts 18 lands and 15 blue sources. That is in line with the archetype's average of 17.43 lands and 15.86 blue sources (measured).

The 5,000-game simulation showed:
- Mulligan rate: 11.1%.
- Colour OK on turn 1: 96.5%.
- Colour OK on turn 3: 85.3%.
- Flood rate: 0.1%.
- Screw rate: 42%, which is high. The simulation can't count Sink into Stupor as a land, so I read this as overstated, but I haven't measured by how much.
- I asked for lord and Vial readiness by turn 3. The tool reported 20.8% castable and 33.9% in hand. I read that as the simulation's limit: it only models mana, and Vial and Master of the Pearl Trident don't need a normal turn-3 play. It is not a reliable measure of how well the deck plays.

**Sideboard** (15 cards). The current field is led by Broodscale Combo (14.4%), Prowess (9.9%), Energy, Blink, Affinity and Devoted Druid Combo. These choices are my judgment about those matchups, using the card text and the results data.
- **Consign to Memory (4):** it counters triggered abilities and colourless spells. That is useful against Blink, Affinity and Eldrazi Tron. The tool showed it in 824 Prowess lists, 598 Blink lists and 476 Affinity lists over 90 days, and it is useful against Broodscale if its combo relies on triggers (my judgment).
- **Chalice of the Void (4):** it is strong against Eldrazi Tron and Devoted Druid Combo, which are among the top users of Chalice in the data.
- **Force of Negation (4):** it counters noncreature spells. Bring it in against Goryo's Vengeance, Frog, Living End and control decks. Take out creature-heavy or low-impact slots. Be careful on the play, since the free mode only works on the opponent's turn.
- **Subtlety (3):** it is good against Frog and Living End, which both play creature spells. Use it as a flash blocker or tempo play.

**Unverified.** I haven't measured win rates against any specific matchup. The sideboard plan is reasoned from card text and play rates, not from tested results.

results.prompt: Make a fun mono white control deck for Modern leagues.
results.text:
**Mono-White Control for Modern leagues** (a brew, with the mana and shell borrowed from UW Control)

**Plan.** Trade one-for-one with cheap exile removal: Path to Exile, March of Otherworldly Light, Fateful Absence, Skyclave Apparition and Solitude. Use Wrath of the Skies and Doomskar when the opponent overextends. Then land a planeswalker to win: Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Elspeth, Storm Slayer, The Wandering Emperor, or The Eternal Wanderer. Wall of Omens and Inspiring Overseer replace cards as you trade, and Castle Ardenvale makes late-game chump blockers.

**Why these cards.** Solitude can be pitched for free or hard-cast. This is the interactive, fun part of the deck, and it works because every card in the deck is white. The Wandering Emperor has flash, so you can pass with four mana open and exile an attacker. Skyclave Apparition and Solitude both come back with Restoration Angel, which also dodges your own sorcery-speed sweepers.

**What I changed in review.**
- **Ephemerate → main-deck Restoration Angel.** Ephemerate needs a creature already on the battlefield. The Angel works on its own and gives the deck a flash threat. This is judgment, not measured.
- **Sideboard:** one Restoration Angel became a third Celestial Purge. Red and black permanents show up in Prowess, Goryo's Vengeance and Broodscale Combo lists.
- **Land count tested.** I simulated cutting to 22 lands. Mulligans rose from 16.8% to 19.3% and screw from 8.7% to 10.5%, so I kept 23.

**Mana (simulated, 5,000 games).**
- The deck has 23 lands: 18 Plains, 3 Castle Ardenvale, Eiganjo and Memorial to Glory. All 23 make white, and white was available on time in every simulated game.
- Mulligan rate was 16.8%, screw 8.7% and flood 2.6%.
- It averages 3.57 lands on turn 4.
- Only 6.8% of games had one of my tracked engine cards castable on turn 4 in the simulation. That figure ignores free Solitude evokes and Wall of Omens draws, and the simulator doesn't model card abilities, so it understates the deck.
- Castle Ardenvale is colourless-free, but Memorial to Glory enters tapped.

**Worst matchups** (shares are from the 30-day meta results; the matchup calls are my judgment):
- **Broodscale Combo (14.4%).** It is the biggest threat. Its cheap threats and Eldrazi Temple let it win before your sweepers matter.
  - Your outs are Path, Skyclave, Solitude and March. Side in Damping Sphere and Orim's Chant, plus Celestial Purge for its black cards.
- **Prowess (9.9%).** Burn plus cheap creatures punishes slow hands.
  - Side in Celestial Purge and Sanctifier en-Vec, which has protection from red and black. Kicked Orim's Chant can also stop one big attack. Keep the cheap removal and the Walls.
- **Storm (3.7%).** Side in Orim's Chant and Damping Sphere. Keep Solitude and Skyclave as flexible answers.
- **Goryo's Vengeance (3.7%).** Side in Rest in Peace and Celestial Purge. Hold Path or Solitude for the reanimated creature.
- **Affinity (5.4%).** Wrath of the Skies and Doomskar are good here, with Stony Silence and Damping Sphere in from the board.
- **Energy (6.1%), Blink (5.9%), Eldrazi Tron (4.9%) and Domain Zoo (4%).** These are playable. Rest in Peace and Celestial Purge cover parts of them. I didn't test these matchups.

**Sideboard (15).** 2 Rest in Peace, 3 Celestial Purge, 2 Stony Silence, 2 Damping Sphere, 2 Sanctifier en-Vec, 2 Orim's Chant, 1 Wrath of the Skies, 1 Restoration Angel.

**Unverified.**
- Matchup strength is my judgment from the archetype lists, not from any simulation.
- Stony Silence is the narrowest sideboard card. Only 4 recent lists run it. It is for Affinity and the artifact lists, so cut one copy if your league doesn't have them.
- Swords to Plowshares and Council's Judgment aren't legal in Modern (checked), so Path to Exile is the only 1-mana exile spell.

intent.goal: Deliver a fun, playable mono white control deck for Modern that works well in league play.

engine.thesis: Mono-white control that trades cheap exile-based removal and flexible sweepers for time, then lands a planeswalker (Elspeth) that wins the game by itself. Mono-white keeps the mana perfect and lets Solitude be pitched or hard-cast, which is the fun, interactive part of the deck.
engine.winCondition: Resolve Elspeth, Sun's Champion or Elspeth, Storm Slayer (backed by The Eternal Wanderer or Elspeth Conquers Death) after a sweeper or removal stabilises the board, then win with soldier tokens and fliers.

Affinity and Energy decks, via Wrath of the Skies and cheap exile
Eldrazi Tron and Domain Zoo midrange
Creature combo shells such as Devoted Druid, via Path and Solitude
losesTo: Broodscale Combo and Storm, because white has almost no counterspells or disruption
Fast starts that beat the sweeper plan before turn 4
Graveyard combo such as Goryo's Vengeance, unless Solitude or Path answers the target

**Sideboard for your Dimir Tempo list (Legacy)**

Your main deck is card-for-card the 5-0 Legacy League list from the archetype data, so I left all 60 untouched and built only the 15.

**Sideboard (15)**
- 3 Consign to Memory
- 2 Force of Negation
- 2 Barrowgoyf
- 2 Hydroblast
- 2 Bloodchief's Thirst
- 2 Surgical Extraction
- 1 Massacre
- 1 Nihil Spellbomb

**Plan:** The main deck stays a cheap-threat tempo deck backed by Daze, Force of Will and Wasteland. The board gives you narrow answers to the decks that beat that plan. All of it is cheap or free, so it fits a deck that wants to keep mana for counterspells.

**Why these cards:**
- **Consign to Memory (3):** It counters triggered abilities or colorless spells. The tool shows it mostly in OmniTell, Blink and Sneak and Show lists. In the meta data, Tron is 7.1%, Eldrazi Aggro 6.1%, OmniTell 4.4%, Blink 3.8% and Sneak and Show 2.5%. It also answers Ocelot Aggro's triggers. Nearly every Dimir list (98.2%) runs it in the board.
- **Force of Negation (2):** It counters noncreature spells for free on the opponent's turn. It is aimed at Doomsday (5.8%), Tron, Izzet Tempo, Storm, Beanstalk and Blink. The tool shows it popular in Doomsday, Tron, Izzet and Blink lists.
- **Hydroblast (2):** Ocelot Aggro is the second-biggest deck at 9%, and its sideboards play Pyroblast (84.6%). Its red cards include Amped Raptor and Goblin Bombardment. Hydroblast also hits Izzet Tempo (4.6%). The reference list ran 1; I went to 2 because those two decks add up to roughly 13.6% of the field.
- **Bloodchief's Thirst (2):** It kills Ocelot Pride, Guide of Souls, Ajani (a mana-value-2 planeswalker) and Death and Taxes creatures. Kicked, it kills a bigger creature or planeswalker late. It supplements your 4 Fatal Push.
- **Barrowgoyf (2):** It has deathtouch and lifelink, so it holds off aggro like Ocelot, Eldrazi and Death and Taxes and wins grindy games against GX Midrange. The reference list ran 3. I cut one so the slots could go to the graveyard cards.
- **Massacre (1):** It is free when the opponent controls a Plains and you control a Swamp. Ocelot Aggro and Death and Taxes play Plains, so it can sweep their small creatures. It also shrinks your own Bowmasters and Tamiyo, so I kept it to 1.
- **Surgical Extraction (2) and Nihil Spellbomb (1):** These are the graveyard hate for Reanimator (3.8%), Sewer Combo (3.4%) and Hogaak (2%). Surgical costs no mana, which suits your tempo plan. Spellbomb replaces itself. I skipped Leyline of the Void, which the reference list ran as 4. It is dead if you draw it late, and I judged one fewer dead slot against the 9.2% of graveyard decks was the better deal.

**Sideboarding:**
- **Ocelot Aggro, Death and Taxes:** Bring in Massacre, Bloodchief's Thirst, Hydroblast (Ocelot only) and Barrowgoyf. Take out Daze and Thoughtseize, whose value drops against cheap creatures.
- **Tron, Eldrazi Aggro:** Bring in Consign to Memory. Add Force of Negation against Tron. Take out Fatal Push and Bloodchief's Thirst-type removal.
- **Doomsday, Storm, Beanstalk, OmniTell, Sneak and Show, Blink:** Bring in Force of Negation and Consign to Memory. Take out the slow or situational creature removal.
- **Izzet Tempo:** Bring in Hydroblast, plus Consign to Memory if they run colorless or trigger-based cards.
- **Reanimator, Sewer Combo, Hogaak:** Bring in Surgical Extraction and Nihil Spellbomb. Take out cards that do little against them, such as Wasteland-heavy draws.
- **GX Midrange:** Bring in Barrowgoyf and Bloodchief's Thirst.

**Mana (measured on the main deck):** In 5,000 simulated games the mulligan rate was 8.7%. Colored mana was available in 86.5% of games by turn 2 and 87.6% by turn 3. Screw rate was 29.2%, and average lands in play were 2.5 by turn 3. This matches the reference list exactly, because the main deck is the same. check_deck reports 19 lands, against an archetype mean of 18.94, and the tool recommends about 20. I left that alone since you asked for a sideboard only.

**Label:** Tuned. The main deck is the stock 5-0 list. The sideboard borrows the Dimir archetype's most common cards, adjusted to the meta shares above.

**Unverified:** I did not check the Sewer Combo and Hogaak lists directly. Treating them as graveyard-reliant decks is my judgment from their names and the tool listing Surgical Extraction and Spellbomb in Hogaak lists.

I replaced it with 2 Chain Lightning and 2 Reckless Lackey, which are both mono-red. Lackey is a 1-mana haste, first-strike creature. This is my judgment, not a tested swap. Losing the Emissary's free mana probably makes Rally turns a little less explosive.

results.prompt: Build a Pioneer deck around Greasefang, Okiba Boss that isn't the usual list.
results.text:
This is an Orzhov vehicle-value deck built around Greasefang. It is a brew that borrows Greasefang's mana base and interaction suite. It does not run Parhelion II, Esika's Chariot or the other usual Greasefang cards.

**Plan.** Cast cheap crew bodies (Virus Beetle, Skyclave Apparition, Murderous Rider) and Smuggler's Copter. Get a vehicle into the graveyard through Copter loots, Carrion Cruiser's mill, or discarding it to Bitter Triumph. Then Greasefang returns a vehicle at the start of every combat, and that vehicle's enters-the-battlefield effect fires again each turn.
- Skysovereign deals 3 damage to a creature or planeswalker.
- Demonic Junker destroys a creature.
- The Fire Nation Drill destroys a creature with power 4 or less.
- Carrion Cruiser refills your hand.

**Why these cards.**
- **Copter and Carrion Cruiser:** Copter loots, and Cruiser mills two cards and returns a creature or vehicle to your hand. Together they put vehicles in the graveyard on purpose.
- **Skysovereign, Junker and Drill:** These are the removal-on-a-stick payoffs. Junker is rarely cast for its full cost, but Greasefang puts it into play at no cost.
- **Virus Beetle and Skyclave Apparition:** These give you crew bodies that also take a card or remove a permanent.
- **Spot removal:** Fatal Push, Bitter Triumph and Murderous Rider protect Greasefang's turn.

**Changes after the matchup review.**
- I cut one Thoughtseize for a main-deck Vanishing Verse. Prowess decks make up about 21.6% of the field in the meta tool, and Thoughtseize costs life against burn. Verse exiles monocolored creatures like Screaming Nemesis, Sheoldred and Professor Dellian Fel.
- I changed the basics from 4 Swamp and 2 Plains to 3 and 3. Skyclave needs WW, and the deck has 20 white and 20 black sources.
- I replaced the 3 Doorkeeper Thrull in the sideboard. Thrull stops enters-the-battlefield triggers, which would shut off your own Cruiser, Skysovereign and Apparition. I replaced them with Cathar Commando and a Thoughtseize and Fatal Push.

**Mana.** The deck has 24 lands and 36 spells, and the check shows no errors or warnings. The simulation gave:

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Mulligan rate | 15.1% |
| Land drops through turn 4 | 70.2% |
| Mana screw | 6.9% |
| Flood | 3.7% |
| Right colors on turn 3 | 96.1% |
| Right colors on turn 4 | 97.7% |
| Greasefang, a reanimation target and an early crew body all ready by turn 4 | 19.6% |
| Those three groups in hand (not necessarily castable) by turn 4 | 33.7% |

The 19.6% shows this deck does not reliably assemble the full engine by turn 4. Treat it as a grindy midrange deck that gets there by turn 5 or 6. The simulator does not model card abilities like Copter loots, so the real numbers should be somewhat better.

**Matchups.**
- **Mono-Red and Izzet Prowess (about 10.8% each):** These are probably the hardest matchups, because burn kills a 3-toughness Greasefang and they race you before the engine runs. Bring in Pest Control, which destroys MV≤1 permanents, so it hits the 1-drops (Monastery Swiftspear, Soul-Scar Mage). Also bring in the extra Vanishing Verse and Fatal Push. Take out 1 Thoughtseize, 1 Demonic Junker and 1 From Father to Son.
- **Golgari Midrange (11.4%):** They play Unlicensed Hearse in 84.5% of sideboards, and the sideboard average is 2.2 copies. That is the real threat to Greasefang here. Vehicles dodge their sorcery-speed removal, though. Bring in Duress, the extra Thoughtseize, Vanishing Verse and Cathar Commando, which can destroy their Hearse.
- **Jund Sacrifice:** I did not pull their list. My judgment is that your recurring removal and card advantage grind them out.
- **Cauldron (7.2%):** They run Agatha's Soul Cauldron, which is colorless, so Verse can't hit it. Bring in Cathar Commando and Loran of the Third Path to destroy it, plus Duress and Thoughtseize. Skyclave Apparition can also exile it.
- **Greasefang mirror (7%):** Bring in Vanishing Verse and Loran. Do not bring in Doorkeeper Thrull.

**Unverified.**
- The turn-by-turn matchup results are judgment, not simulated. The simulator only measures mana and draws.
- I did not pull the Jund Sacrifice list.
- The deck has no maindeck answer to graveyard hate beyond redundancy in Cruiser and Copter.

results.prompt: Make a Vintage artifact aggro deck.
results.text:
This is Raker Shops, a Mishra's Workshop artifact deck. It's the most recent 5-0 Vintage League list for that strategy, submitted unchanged as **stock**. I picked it because it is the artifact-based aggro strategy in the results. Raker Shops is 9.1% of the recent field (61 lists), and the archetype tool shows lists that run Workshop, Ancient Tomb and Glaring Fleshraker every time.

**Plan:** Cast threats a turn or two early off Moxen, Mana Crypt, Sol Ring, Grim Monolith and the Workshop and Tomb lands. Glaring Fleshraker and Tezzeret, Cruel Captain turn each artifact into value or damage. Scrawling Crawler and The Fantasticar are the main clock, with Time Vault, Mystic Forge and Karn, the Great Creator as extra power. Chalice of the Void, Trinisphere, Wasteland and Strip Mine slow the opponent.

**Why the key cards** (from the archetype data):
- **Glaring Fleshraker** is in 100% of Raker Shops lists at 4 copies. It makes Spawn tokens whenever you cast a colorless spell and pings the opponent when another colorless creature enters.
- **Tezzeret, Cruel Captain** is in 97.7% of lists at 4 copies. It gains loyalty from each artifact, untaps your artifacts, and can fetch a 0- or 1-cost artifact.
- **Scrawling Crawler** is a 3/2 that makes each player draw an extra card and makes the opponent lose 1 life per draw. Its adoption is only 32.7% in the archetype data, but this list plays 4.
- **The Fantasticar** is a 4/4 flier you can make a creature when you cast a noncreature spell.

**Mana:**
- The list has 18 lands. `check_deck` passed it, with an average mana value of 1.76 and 10 zero-cost cards.
- It also noted that Raker Shops lists average 15.4 lands, so this is above average. That is a deliberate choice in the winning list: Workshop, Tomb and Talon Gates are effectively mana sources.
- The simulation matched the reference list. Mulligan rate was 8.6% and colored mana was fine every turn, but the simulator only counts lands. Mulligan rate and land-drop numbers for the deck are therefore measured. The deck's real speed, which comes from Moxen, Crypt, Lotus and Monolith, is not measured.
- The "screw rate" of 32.8% and the "engine ready by turn 3" figure of 12.7% understate the deck because of that.

**Sideboard** (as in the 5-0 list: 3 Argentum Masticore, 2 Dismember, 1 Grafdigger's Cage, 1 Karakas, 2 Karn, Scion of Urza, 4 Null Rod, 1 Pithing Needle, 1 Stonecoil Serpent). These plans are my judgment, not measured:
- **Versus Lurrus Control, Lurrus PO and Paradoxical Outcome:**
  - Bring in the Null Rods and Pithing Needle against their artifact mana and permanents; the Grafdigger's Cage in the main deck and side also helps against graveyard plays.
  - Karn, Scion of Urza gives you card advantage against slower control.
  - Take out the weakest or most expensive cards, such as Time Vault and Mystic Forge.
  - Null Rod also shuts off your own artifacts, so only bring it in if the matchup justifies it.
- **Versus Mono-White Initiative and other creature decks:** Dismember, Argentum Masticore and Stonecoil Serpent help block and remove attackers. Karakas can bounce a legendary creature.
- **Versus Oath and Tinker:** Dismember and Karakas handle the big creatures they cast.
- **Versus Dredge:** Grafdigger's Cage is the only graveyard hate in the sideboard.

**Unverified:** I did not check the opponent matchups against the field with a tool. I also did not re-check the sideboard cards' rules text, so the matchup advice above is judgment.

results.prompt: Give me a strong Golgari midrange list for Standard.
results.text:
**Golgari Midrange (stock)** is submitted and accepted. It is the most recent list from the Golgari Midrange archetype: Standard Challenge 16, 2026-10-11, which finished 1-3 and placed 32nd. I changed nothing. That list is a weak result, and the archetype has only 9 lists in the data, so Golgari is a minor strategy here. The largest strategies in the meta are Jund Sacrifice at 11.2%, Dimir Midrange at 9.7% and Elementals at 9.5%.

**Plan:** Ramp with Environmental Scientist and Simulacrum Shaper, which fetch basic lands. Then land planeswalkers and Vraska, the Cutting Glare, and answer threats with cheap removal. Vraska's destroy trigger needs six lands, so the land-fetching creatures help turn it on.

**Key cards**
- **Vraska, the Cutting Glare (4):** A 4/4 deathtouch for 3 mana. If you control six or more lands, it also destroys target permanent an opponent controls. They get a Treasure.
- **Professor Dellian Fel (3):** Gains life, draws cards, or destroys a creature for 3 loyalty.
- **Garruk, Veiled Butcher (2) and Garruk, Curse Breaker (2):** The Butcher makes opponents discard or sacrifice. The Curse Breaker makes 4/4 Beasts and draws a card whenever a creature with power 4 or more enters.
- **Ral Zarek, Guest Lecturer (2):** Surveils, makes players discard, and can reanimate a creature with mana value 3 or less.
- **Removal:** Requiting Hex (3), Shoot the Sheriff (2), Bitter Triumph (2), Witherbloom Charm (4) and Maelstrom Pulse (2) cover cheap and expensive threats. Witherbloom Charm can also draw two cards or gain 5 life.
- **Emeritus of Abundance (3):** A 3/4 vigilance body for 3 mana.

**Mana:** 24 lands: 4 Ba Sing Se, 4 Deathcap Glade, 4 Overgrown Tomb, 4 Wastewood Verge, 5 Swamp and 3 Forest. The check shows 17 black and 19 green sources. Real Golgari lists average 18.2 black and 20.3 green. Land count matches the archetype average of 24.3.

The simulation (5,000 games) gave these numbers:
- Mulligan rate: 15.9%.
- Screw rate: 7.7%.
- Flood rate: 3.6%.
- Lands in play by turn 4: 3.63 on average.
- Colors OK by turn 3: 83.8%.
- Colors OK by turn 4: 91.3%.
- At least one of Environmental Scientist or Simulacrum Shaper in hand by turn 4: 71.8%. Castable by turn 4: 67.8%.

**Sideboard (15):** 4 Duress, 4 Vicious Rivalry, 2 Strategic Betrayal, 2 Outrageous Robbery, 2 Ghost Vacuum, 1 Maelstrom Pulse. The matchup notes below are my judgment, not measured.
- **Control (4C, Azorius, Sultai):** Bring in Duress, Outrageous Robbery and Strategic Betrayal. Take out the narrow cheap removal, such as Requiting Hex.
- **Creature-heavy aggro (Boros Dragons, Prowess, Landfall):** Bring in Vicious Rivalry as a sweeper. Take out the discard-oriented cards, such as Ral and the Garruks.
- **Reanimator, Lessons, Elementals and other graveyard decks:** Bring in Ghost Vacuum and Strategic Betrayal, which exile graveyards.

results.prompt: Make a Legacy deck that wins on turn 1 every game.
results.text:
No Legacy deck can win on turn 1 every game. Mulligans are part of every game, and the sims show a real share of hands with no way to act. Opponents also get to disrupt you. On the draw, the opponent's turn 1 comes first. The closest real deck is The Epic Storm, which I submitted as a brew. Treat its turn-1 kills as an occasional result, not a promise.

**Why not the other fast decks**
- **Sneak and Show:** I sim-tested the 5-0 list for a turn-1 combo and got 0% "engine ready" (Show and Tell, a big creature and fast mana together). Its payoffs also don't end the game on their own. By the card text, Emrakul gives an extra turn but only has 15 power, and Atraxa just draws cards. That makes it a turn-2-or-later deck.
- **Reanimator:** Griselbrand draws cards but doesn't win by itself.
- **Epic Storm:** it is the only archetype I checked whose payoff, Tendrils of Agony, can end the game from one hand. The chain runs on rituals, free mana and tutors.

**The deck**
- **Plan:** Mulligan toward a hand with a ritual or free mana, a tutor, and Lion's Eye Diamond. Chain the cheap spells into a lethal Tendrils of Agony. If that chain isn't there, play a turn-2 or turn-3 storm turn.
- **Free mana:** 4 each of Lotus Petal, Chrome Mox, Mox Opal, Lion's Eye Diamond and Dark Ritual. The average mana value is 1.13.
- **Tutors and disruption:** Burning Wish ×3, Infernal Tutor ×4, Beseech the Mirror ×2, Gaea's Will, Thoughtseize ×4 and Duress ×3. Ad Nauseam and Wishclaw Talisman are backup payoffs.
- **Lands:** 14.

**Odds (measured)**
- **Hand quality:** In 5,000 simulated games the deck mulliganed 15.1% of the time. It had 52.6% "screw" by that sim's definition, which is common for a deck this light on lands and leaning on artifact mana.
- **Turn-1 setup:** The sim saw all three engine groups ready on turn 1 only 2.7% of the time. That sim doesn't model card abilities, so it undercounts. The same measurement shows that "ready" is a very small slice.
- **Opening 7 on the play:** 74.1% to see at least one of the 10 tutors, and 39.9% each for Lion's Eye Diamond and for Dark Ritual. All three together is 9.4%.
- **Real turn-1 win rate:** I have no measured number for it. My judgment is that it is a small single-digit percentage, with the exact figure depending on how well you pilot it.

**Sideboarding (judgment, from the sideboard in the list I borrowed)**
- **Graveyard hate and combo decks:** Boomerang Basics ×4, Hexing Squelcher ×2 and Veil-style protection in the main deck help against counterspells and discard.
- **Where Leyline of the Void ×4 goes:** It stays in the sideboard against Reanimator.
- **Backup kill:** Tendrils of Agony ×1 and Peer into the Abyss ×1 are Wish targets.
- **Plan B:** Debt to the Deathless and the extra Beseech the Mirror give alternate Wish targets.

**Status:** This is a brew that borrows its shell from the 5-2 Legacy Challenge list for The Epic Storm. The 60 main cards and the sideboard are identical to that list, so I made no changes of my own.

**Unverified:** I didn't look up the rules text of the storm payoffs, such as Tendrils of Agony or Lion's Eye Diamond, or run a turn-1 kill sim. The 52.6% screw figure is the sim's definition and could be misleading for this deck. I also didn't measure how often Epic Storm wins in actual games.

intent.goal: Recognize that no Legacy deck can win on turn 1 in every game, since mulligans, disruption, and the player going second make it unachievable, and explain this honestly.

results.prompt: Build a Timeless reanimator deck.
results.text:
This is a brew, not a stock list. The tools have no Timeless results, so I borrowed the Legacy Reanimator shell. Most of the Legacy staples aren't legal in Timeless, so I rebuilt around the cards that are. The deck passed `check_deck` and was accepted. The simulation was not a clean pass (see Mana).

**Plan.** Put Griselbrand or Atraxa into the graveyard on turn 1 or 2, then bring it back with Reanimate or Necromancy. Dark Ritual makes the turn-1 play possible. Thoughtseize, Inquisition and Collective Brutality strip the opponent's answers first.

**Why these cards**
- **Reanimation, 8 copies:** Reanimate ×4 and Necromancy ×4. The tool confirms both are legal.
  - Animate Dead, Shallow Grave, Exhume, Goryo's Vengeance and Archon of Cruelty are not legal in Timeless. Necromancy replaces Animate Dead, and it can be cast with flash.
  - Reanimate costs life equal to the creature's mana value, so it loses 8 life on Griselbrand. Necromancy costs no life.
- **Graveyard fillers:** Entomb ×4, Buried Alive, Stitcher's Supplier ×4, Faithless Looting ×4. Troll of Khazad-dûm can be discarded for a Swamp.
- **Targets:** Griselbrand ×4, Atraxa ×3 and Raph & Mikey ×1, plus Troll as a ninth body. Atraxa is only ever reanimated, so its four colours don't matter. Raph & Mikey has haste and trample.
- **Backup threats:** Bloodghast ×2 can be discarded to Looting and comes back with land drops.
- **Acceleration and disruption:** Dark Ritual ×4, Thoughtseize ×4, Inquisition ×2, Collective Brutality ×2. Lotus Petal and Unmask are not legal.

**Mana.**
- The deck runs 16 lands: 4 Bloodstained Mire, 2 Polluted Delta, 2 Blood Crypt, 2 Raucous Theater, 4 Swamp, 1 Mountain and 1 Urborg.
- The 16 lands match the Legacy Reanimator average of 14.6 (measured). `check_deck` warns that a deck with this curve would normally run about 22 lands. I kept 16 because the deck is built around 1-mana spells.
- `check_deck` counts 15 black sources and 9 red sources. Red is only needed for Looting.
- In the 5,000-game simulation, 11.1% of hands needed a mulligan. Black and red colour requirements were met 80% of the time by turn 1, 88% by turn 2 and 92% by turn 5.
- The simulation reported a 42% screw rate and only about 2.7 lands in play on turn 4. That is thin, so expect some non-functional draws.
- Its "engine ready on turn 2" figure came back as 0%, so I can't cite a turn-2 combo rate. At least one engine piece was in hand about 34% of the time by turn 2.

**Sideboard.** It has 15 cards: Faerie Macabre ×3, Duress ×2, Bitter Triumph ×2, Fatal Push ×2, Dauthi Voidwalker ×2, Collective Brutality ×2 and Abrade ×2.
- **Against graveyard hate:** The deck has no way to fight it itself. Faerie Macabre and Dauthi Voidwalker help against graveyard decks. Dauthi stops an opponent reanimating your fatties out of their graveyard.
- **Against combo and control:** Add Duress, and take out the slower Atraxa copies if you want more room.
- **Against creature and artifact decks:** Bring in Push, Triumph and Abrade, and cut a few Inquisitions or Brutalities.

**Unverified.** Nothing here was tested against the Timeless field. The sideboard split is my judgment, not tournament data. The Legacy Reanimator results I borrowed from also show Show and Tell in 86% of sideboards, which I left out here.

results.prompt: Make an Elves deck for Historic.
results.text:
This is a brew, not a proven list. I found no Elves results for Historic, and none for Pioneer or Standard either. The `meta` tool returned no Historic data, and `archetype` found no Elves strategy in any of the three formats.

I borrowed only the generic parts from Pioneer. Mono-Green Devotion and Selesnya Company both run 4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Elvish Mystic, Collected Company or Boseiju. The Elves tribal core is my own build from the Historic card pool.

**Plan:** Mono-green Elves. Turn 1 and 2 mana elves feed Imperious Perfect, Elvish Archdruid, Elvish Warmaster and the other lords. Elvish Archdruid and Priest of Titania make a lot of mana off the Elf count. The deck then wins with a wide, pumped board, with Craterhoof Behemoth as the one-of finisher.

**Key cards:**
- **Elvish Warmaster and Imperious Perfect:** both make Elf Warrior tokens, so the board keeps growing.
- **Priest of Titania and Elvish Archdruid:** both tap for G for each Elf, and they are the mana engine.
- **Collected Company:** puts two Elves with mana value 3 or less onto the battlefield at instant speed.
- **Cavern of Souls (3):** I assumed naming Elf here makes Elf spells uncounterable. That helps against blue decks.
- **Leaf-Crowned Visionary and Dwynen, Gilt-Leaf Daen:** more Elf pump and card draw.

**Banned or not legal:** Veil of Summer is banned in Historic. Heritage Druid, Elvish Harbinger and Gilt-Leaf Archdruid are not legal.

**Mana:** 21 lands, which are 17 Forest, 3 Cavern of Souls and Boseiju, plus 8 one-mana elves. `check_deck` passed with no errors and reports 26 green sources.

| Simulation (5,000 games) | 22 lands | 20 lands | 21 lands (submitted) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mulligan rate | 19.3% | 8.4% | 8.7% |
| Stuck on lands (screw) | 10.5% | 25.6% | 21.8% |

- The 21-land build had 0.7% flood, and colour was fine every turn because the deck is mono-green.
- The simulator doesn't model mana elves, so the screw figure is pessimistic.
- The 22-land build also had 2% flood.
- The "engine ready" numbers didn't come out usable, so I'm not citing them.
- 21 lands is a judgment call between the two.

**Sideboard (15):**
- **Reclamation Sage (2), Nature's Claim (2), Haywire Mite (2):** artifact and enchantment answers. Use them against Cauldron, Greasefang, UW Control and other artifact or enchantment decks.
- **Tail Swipe (3):** cheap removal for Prowess and other aggro decks.

results.prompt: Make a Penny Dreadful burn deck.
results.text:
This is a mono-red burn deck, and it's a brew rather than a proven list. The tools returned no Penny Dreadful results, so I couldn't take a top-finishing list as the base. The meta tool pointed to Pauper and Modern. Pauper has no burn strategy in its results. Modern Burn has a list, but most of its core cards aren't legal here. Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning, Rift Bolt, Skewer the Critics, Lava Spike, Goblin Guide, Swiftspear, Eidolon and Boros Charm all showed as not legal. I kept Modern Burn's structure (cheap creatures plus a pile of 2–4 damage burn) and rebuilt it from cards the tools showed as legal.

**Plan:** Get early damage from Vexing Devil, Keldon Marauders and Viashino Pyromancer. Then burn the opponent out with 3–4 damage spells, using the same spells to remove blockers when needed. Hellrider is a haste finisher. Sulfuric Vortex punishes slower decks and stops lifegain.

**Key cards:**
- **Vexing Devil, Keldon Marauders and Viashino Pyromancer:** Each deals direct damage even if it gets blocked or removed.
- **Searing Spear, Lightning Strike, Burst Lightning and Shock:** These are the efficient burn, and all can hit a creature or the opponent. Burst Lightning kicks for 4 late in the game.
- **Char:** It deals 4 damage as a finisher or removal.
- **Bonecrusher Giant (Stomp):** It's removal early and a 4/3 body later.
- **Arc Lightning, Magma Jet and Fireball:** These round out the burn and handle small creatures.

**Mana:** The deck has 17 Mountains and no color issues, since it is all red. The simulation (5,000 games, target turn 3) measured:
- **Mulligans:** 9.8% of games.
- **Colors:** Colored mana was available 100% of the time.
- **Opening hands:** The engine (a cheap creature plus a burn spell) was in hand 82.3% of the time. It was castable by turn 3 in 74.7% of games.
- **Lands:** The simulation reported a 38.1% screw rate. The tool doesn't define that figure here, so treat it as a caution. I'd keep 17 lands rather than cut to 16.
- **Land-count warning:** check_deck suggested about 23 lands, but that is a generic estimate. I'm treating it as not applicable to a deck averaging 2.02 mana value with a mana-sink finisher (kicker, Char).

**Sideboard:**
- **Smash to Smithereens (2):** Bring these in against artifact decks like Affinity.
- **Pyroclasm (2) and Goblin Chainwhirler (2):** Bring these in against creature swarms like Elves and Mono-White Aggro. Take out Vexing Devil and Sulfuric Vortex.
- **Thunderbolt (2):** It deals 4 damage to a flyer, so it's good against Faeries.
- **Collective Defiance, Barbed Lightning and Mizzium Mortars:** These add removal against bigger creatures, and Collective Defiance can also go to the face.
- **Banefire (2):** A flexible finisher against slow, controlling decks.

The Pauper meta shares (Madness 16.5%, Terror 8.6%, Faeries 8.3%) are from Pauper, not Penny Dreadful, so I used them only as a rough guide. Pairing opponent decks with sideboard cards is my judgment, since there is no Penny Dreadful matchup data. Card counts and the exact sideboard split haven't been tested against real results.

results.text:
**Verdict:** I resubmitted the deck with two changes, and it was accepted as a brew. Its worst matchups are Broodscale and Prowess. Its worst weakness is mana.

**Plan.** "Scam" isn't a card in the pool. I read it as the evoke-Elemental shell: Deceit, Shriekmaw, Subtlety and Endurance. Cascade (Shardless Agent, Violent Outburst, Demonic Dread) puts Living End on the stack. Living End has mana value 0, so it is the only card those cascades can hit. The evoke Elementals and Street Wraith fill the graveyard with big creatures first, and Shriekmaw's removal trigger fires again when it returns. Subtlety and Endurance protect the turn.

**Changes from the submitted list.**
- **Force of Negation:** I added 1 to the main deck, replacing the second Oliphaunt. Force of Negation is a counterspell for noncreature spells. It is the best answer to Broodscale's noncreature spells. The tools show Broodscale (14.4% of the field) running Kozilek's Command and Malevolent Rumble. Force of Negation also appears in 100% of the Living End lists the tool returned, usually as 4 copies.
- **Sideboard:** it already held 3 Force of Negation. I moved 1 into the main deck and the other 2 stay as sideboard cards, since a counterspell is dead against creature-heavy decks.
- **Wistfulness:** I wanted 2 in the main deck, but the main deck can't go above 60% overlap with an existing Living End list. Wistfulness is 100% of those lists, so I dropped it.
- **Curator of Mysteries:** I wanted to cut it to 1, but the locked engine needs 2.

**Mana.** The tools returned these numbers for the final 16-land list with 4 Street Wraith:
- The simulation (5,000 games) gives an 11.1% mulligan rate and 42% screw. The lands drop to 2.72 in play by turn 4.
- Color access is the soft spot. I measured 79% on turn 3 for the revised 16-land version, against 86.8% for a real Living End list.
- I did not simulate the final submitted list, only the 16-land revised variant. The final list should be about the same, but that is judgment.
- The cause is Demonic Dread (needs B and R), because it makes the deck four-colour. I can't fix that without changing the locked engine.
- A 17th land made colors worse (74.7% on turn 3). A basic Island doesn't help the three coloured cascade spells.
- Blue sources are only 8, against about 10.4 in real lists. Treat this as the main risk.
- The simulator measures land drops and colors only. The "engine ready by turn 3" figure was 14.2%. Cascade creatures in hand by turn 3 was 40.4%.

**Matchups, from the meta data.**
- **Broodscale (14.4%):** a hard matchup. Their turn-3-or-4 plan is mostly noncreature spells, so Force of Negation and Mystical Dispute help. Subtlety can hit Emrakul, but I didn't verify that interaction.
- **Prowess (9.9%):** also hard. Lightning Bolt and Lava Dart kill our cascade creature, and they board Tormod's Crypt and Surgical Extraction (47% and 48.6% of Prowess lists). Living End does sweep their creatures. Hold Endurance and Subtlety as blockers.
- **Others:** Energy, Blink and Affinity are untested. I'd expect Affinity to be better after boarding Foundation Breaker, Force of Vigor and Damping Sphere (judgment, not measured).

**Sideboarding.**
- **Against Broodscale and Goryo's Vengeance:** bring in Force of Negation, Mystical Dispute, and Inevitable Betrayal if they keep creatures in the deck.
- **Against Affinity:** bring in Force of Vigor, Foundation Breaker and Damping Sphere. Damping Sphere also helps against Storm.
- **Against Prowess:** bring in Dismember for their early creatures. Keep Endurance in the deck to turn off their graveyard plan. Cut Curator of Mysteries and Troll of Khazad-dûm, which are too slow.
- **Against graveyard hate and counterspells:** keep Subtlety and the Force of Negation copies, and cut the clunky big creatures.

**Label.** This is a brew. It borrows the Living End shell: 4 each of Endurance, Subtlety, Shardless Agent, Violent Outburst and Street Wraith, plus the usual dual lands and fetches.

**Unverified.** I have not measured win rates against any matchup. The matchup assessments are judgment based on the meta data.

results.prompt: Build a Pauper deck around Kiln Fiend.
results.text:
**Plan.** Cast cheap spells to pump Kiln Fiend, which gets +3/+0 for each one. Then give it double strike with Temur Battle Rage or Assault Strobe. Fiend plus two spells is 7 power, so 14 damage with double strike. The burn doubles as extra triggers and finishes the game. Expressive Firedancer is a second creature that scales with spells.

**Changes from the submitted list.** I made one swap, Gut Shot for Lava Dart. Gut Shot's 1 damage doesn't kill a 2-toughness Fiend or Firedancer. Lava Dart has flashback (sacrifice a Mountain), so one card is two spell triggers. The Kiln Fiend archetype in tournament results plays four Lava Dart. In the sideboard, 2 Dispel became 2 more Apostle's Blessing. Dispel is hard to cast on 8 blue sources and Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast already cover blue decks. Apostle's Blessing protects Fiend from Terror and other removal (Terror is 8.6% of the field). Archetype lists play four copies across main and side, so this matches.

**Why the key cards**
- **Manamorphose and Mutagenic Growth:** each is a spell trigger that costs no mana or card. Manamorphose replaces itself, and Mutagenic Growth can be paid with 2 life.
- **Ponder and Preordain:** these find Fiend or the double-strike spell. They are the reason to be blue at all.
- **Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning, Burst Lightning, Lava Dart:** removal for early blockers and the finishing damage.

**Mana (17 lands: 9 Mountain, 5 Island, 3 Swiftwater Cliffs).** The simulation covers land drops and colors only, not what the cantrips draw.
- It had 9.6% mulligans, and the correct colors by turn 3 in 76.3% of games.
- A fully set-up engine (creature, double-strike spell and cantrip) was castable by turn 3 in 26.1% of games.
- A creature, a double-strike spell, or a cantrip was in hand by turn 3 in 38.6% of games.
- I also tested 16 lands and heavier red splits (10 Mountain, 3 or 4 Island). Both were worse: colors correct by turn 3 in 70–74% of games, and screw rate rose from 37% to 42% with 16 lands. I kept the original split.
- Honest read: this is a fragile, high-variance deck. Expect to mulligan and to lose some games to colors.

**Matchups.** This is judgment, since I didn't simulate matchups. Meta shares are from tournament results.
- **Better:** Elves, Spy Combo, and slow decks. Lava Dart and Electrickery kill their small creatures.
- **Worst:**
  - Madness (16.5%) is fast, and its Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast hit our blue cantrips. Fiend, a 1/2, also dies to its burn.
  - Terror (8.6%) and Faeries (8.3%) have removal and counterspells.
  - Affinity and Mono-White Aggro race us.

**Sideboard plan**
- **Faeries, Dimir Control, Jeskai Control:** bring in 3 Pyroblast and 3 Red Elemental Blast. Take out Assault Strobe and some Ponder, since a sorcery double-strike spell is clunky into counterspells.
- **Madness, Terror:** bring in the extra 2 Apostle's Blessing to protect Fiend. Take out Chain Lightning or Burst Lightning, but keep the cantrips.
- **Elves, Mono-White Aggro, Bogles, Spy Combo:** bring in 3 Electrickery. Bring in 2 Flaring Pain against Spy Combo and Bogles, because damage can't be prevented. Take out Firedancer.
- **Madness graveyard plans:** 2 Relic of Progenitus.

**Label.** This is a brew. It borrows its core from the Kiln Fiend archetype (Fiend, Temur Battle Rage, Assault Strobe, Manamorphose, Mutagenic Growth, Apostle's Blessing, Lava Dart, the sideboard) and adds a blue cantrip package.

**Unverified.** I didn't measure any matchup win rates. Expressive Firedancer has no tournament results to back it. I haven't checked how often the combo kills on turn 4.

results.prompt: Build me a Premodern Dream Halls deck that doesn't win with storm.
results.text:
**Dream Halls without storm: UW Halls into Akroma (revised submission)**

**Plan.** Resolve Dream Halls, Show and Tell, or Enlightened Tutor for Dream Halls, then put Akroma, Angel of Wrath into play for free. Akroma is a 6/6 flying, first strike, trample, haste creature with protection from black and red. A free Armageddon can clear the way first. Orim's Chant stops the opponent from casting spells, so counterspells can't answer the finisher. There is no Storm, Tendrils or Mind's Desire anywhere in the deck.

**Why the key cards.** All card text below comes from tool results.
- **Dream Halls and Show and Tell:** these are the two engines. You get either one into play, then Akroma follows free, with no mana.
- **Intuition, Enlightened Tutor and Cunning Wish:**
  - Enlightened Tutor can find Dream Halls or Lotus Petal.
  - Intuition puts Eternal Dragon or other cards into the graveyard if the opponent gives you something else. Dragon can return to hand in your upkeep for {3}{W}{W}.
  - Cunning Wish gets an instant from the sideboard, such as a counterspell or Hydroblast.
- **Akroma, Angel of Wrath:** this is the printed 8-mana creature with haste. It comes down and attacks the same turn, and it blanks Sligh's and Goblins' red burn.
- **Eternal Dragon:** a 5/5 flyer and the backup finisher. It can also plainscycle for {2}.
- **Orim's Chant and Swords to Plowshares:**
  - Chant, kicked, also stops attacks. That helps against Sligh.
  - Swords answers Phyrexian Dreadnought, a 100% inclusion in Stiflenought lists.
- **Arcane Denial:** 2.3 copies on average in Dream Halls lists (80% of lists).

**What I changed in review.**
- I cut City of Traitors for a fourth Plains. A land that is sacrificed when you play another land worked against the colours. The simulation shows colours OK by turn 2 rising from 86.4% to 88.2%, and by turn 6 from 93.9% to 95.1%. Turn 1 dipped slightly, from 74.9% to 74.3%.
- I swapped the main-deck Disenchant for Opt. That is smoother and still gives blue discard fodder.
- I moved Disenchant to the sideboard as a second copy, so Cunning Wish can fetch it. I also traded one Mana Leak for a second Annul.

**Mana.** The deck runs 19 lands and 3 Lotus Petal.
- **Lands:** 4 Adarkar Wastes, 2 Flooded Strand, 3 Ancient Tomb, 6 Island, 4 Plains.
- **Simulation (5,000 games):**
  - 8.4% mulligans.
  - 29.4% screw rate.
  - 39.3% landdrops through turn 4.
  - 33.6% of games have an engine card in hand by turn 4.
- **Caveat:** the "engine ready" figure came back 0. The simulator can't model Dream Halls' free casting or the Show and Tell setup, so I can't give a measured turn-4 kill rate. The "turn 4" target is a judgment from the curve.
- **Other cost:** Ancient Tomb deals 2 damage to you and Adarkar Wastes 1, which hurts against Sligh.

**Matchups.** These are judgment calls, not measured win rates.
- **Weakest: Stiflenought (10.4% of the field).** It runs Counterspell, Foil, Daze and Annul, and Annul is a 96.5% sideboard inclusion. Chant is your best answer, though a free Daze can still beat it.
- **Weak: Terrageddon (11.2%).** It runs Disenchant, Swords and its own Armageddon.
- **Favoured: Sligh (9.9%).** Akroma has protection from red, and Chant, Swords and Hydroblast all help.
- **Likely fine: Enchantress (12.5%).** Armageddon plus a hasty flyer should punish it, but it plays Swords. Treat it as untested.

**Sideboarding.** You have 15 cards. Cunning Wish can fetch any instant.
- **Against Sligh, Goblins, Zoo and Oath Ponza:** bring in 2 Hydroblast and 2 Blue Elemental Blast.
- **Against Stiflenought:**
  - Bring in 2 Annul to counter Dreadnought, 2 Chain of Vapor, and 2 Counterspell. Annul is the only Stiflenought answer that deals with Dreadnought as it is cast.
  - Take out Arcane Denial, since it hands them cards. Cut the Opt and Sleight of Hand too if you want more room.
  - Don't bring the red hate in. Stiflenought runs no red.
- **Against Terrageddon and Standstill:** bring in the 2 Disenchant, and Wrath of God against creature decks.
- **Against Hermit Druid and Replenish:** bring in Tormod's Crypt and the counterspells.

**Status.** This is a brew built on the Dream Halls archetype shell. It is not a proven list, because recent results show Dream Halls lists run Meditate, Opportunity and Brain Freeze, which this one avoids on purpose. The matchup read above comes from archetype data and card text, not from played games.

results.prompt: Build a deck that best utilizes Peter Parker's Camera.
results.text:
**Peter Parker's Camera reanimator (Modern, brew, borrowing the Grixis Persist shell)**

**Plan.** Get Archon of Cruelty into the graveyard with Stitcher's Supplier, Faithless Looting, Buried Alive or Troll swampcycling. Reanimate it with Persist or Reanimate, with Camera already in play. Spend {2} to copy the enter trigger, then {2} again to copy the attack trigger. Each trigger makes the opponent sacrifice a creature or planeswalker, discard a card and lose 3 life, while you draw a card and gain 3 life. Camera has only three film counters, so the plan is to use them on Archon.

**What I changed from the submitted list.**
- **Cut Lightning Bolt (2) and 2 Mountains.** Bolt was the only main-deck red card, and the three Mountains hurt the black mana that Troll swampcycling and Archon's {B}{B} need. Black-only mana is better here.
- **Added 1 Bitter Triumph, a Swamp, and a second Swamp in place of the Mountains.** The main deck is now 20 lands: 12 Swamp, 1 Mountain, 3 Blood Crypt, 3 Bloodstained Mire and the Pathway. I added a land because the sim showed 29.4% screw at 19 lands.
- **Sideboard:** I replaced the 3 Terminate with 2 Go for the Throat and 1 Bitter Triumph, which only need black mana. The deck has roughly 8 red sources (Blood Crypts, Pathway, Mires and the Mountain), which should still cast Pyroclasm, Meltdown and Kolaghan's Command. That is judgment, not measured.

**Mana (simulated, 5,000 games).**
- **Mulligans:** 8.4%.
- **Screw rate:** 25.6%, down from 29.4% at 19 lands.
- **Lands in play on turn 4:** 3.13 on average, at 20 lands.
- **Color:** 90.3% of games have the right colors by turn 4. Over the first turns that is 75.0%, 87.1%, 88.1% and 89.2% (turns 1 to 4).
- **Engine:** the sim reports "engine ready" as 0% because it treats Archon as an 8-mana card to cast, so ignore that number. Archon, Persist or Reanimate, or Camera were in hand in 19.7% of games by turn 4.

**Matchups, from the meta data.**
- **Broodscale Combo (14.4%) is the scariest matchup.** It runs 22.67 lands on average and plays Emrakul, the Promised End. Thoughtseize and Inquisition help, and Fatal Push and Bitter Triumph can kill the small creatures. Damping Sphere comes in because their colorless lands (Eldrazi Temple, Urza's Saga) are core. I did not simulate this matchup, so how well it goes is judgment.
- **Prowess (9.9%) is a bad matchup.** Reanimate costs life equal to Archon's mana value, which is 8. Persist is the safer reanimation spell against fast decks. Bring in Pyroclasm, Go for the Throat and Kolaghan's Command. Take out Camera, Buried Alive and Troll.
- **Affinity and Energy** are artifact-heavy, so Meltdown and Kolaghan's Command come in. Camera is fragile against Kolaghan's Command-style artifact removal anyway.
- **Goryo's Vengeance and Living End** both rely on their graveyards. Surgical Extraction comes in for them, and you can also use it on their reanimation targets.
- **Storm and control decks:** bring in Duress, plus Damping Sphere against Storm.
- **Fatal Push** is the main cheap interaction. Take out the clunkiest creature-light cards on the draw if the opponent is fast.

**Unverified.**
- Camera's synergy is my judgment. The tool data shows Camera in only 2 recent lists.
- The 3-turn kill is a goal, not a measured speed.
- Instant-speed removal on Archon in response to the copy would waste a Camera activation.
- Grave Researcher // Reanimate has no recent tournament results, so how it performs is untested.

results.prompt: Build a Commander deck with Atraxa, Praetors' Voice that's all about proliferate.
results.text:
**Atraxa, Praetors' Voice proliferate deck, revised once (brew, borrowing the proliferate/counters shell)**

**Plan.** Land Atraxa on turn 4, or turn 3 with ramp. Atraxa proliferates every end step, and cheap proliferate spells and doublers grow +1/+1 counters, loyalty and poison. Atraxa and the other counter-laden creatures win in combat as a flying, lifelinking body. Planeswalker ultimates (Ajani, Sleeper Agent's poison emblem; Vraska's -9) are the backup finish.

**What I changed in review.** There is no meta data for Commander, so I judged the matchups from the card pool and the locked list's own weaknesses.
- **The weak points.** The deck's worst matchups are fast combo, wraths and mass bounce, and stax or counter-hate. The original had plenty of removal but no way to stop a combo piece or a wrath on the stack. It also ran 36 lands plus about 10 ramp spells, a lot of mana for an average mana value of 3.
- **The swap.** I cut one Forest and one Island, the two colours with spare sources (G and U were at 19.5). I added Fierce Guardianship and Force of Will. Both are free to cast (Guardianship while you control Atraxa; Force by pitching a blue card), so you can hold up protection while still developing.
- **What I left alone.** The engine and the colour balance of the fixing are unchanged.

**Key cards**
- **Repeatable proliferate:** Atraxa herself, Evolution Sage, Thrummingbird, Flux Channeler, Tekuthal, Contagion Engine, Contagion Clasp, Karn's Bastion, Tromell and Ichormoon Gauntlet.
- **Doublers:** Doubling Season, Hardened Scales, Winding Constrictor, Corpsejack Menace, Branching Evolution, Pir and Vorinclex.
- **Planeswalkers:** Ajani, Sleeper Agent, Ajani Steadfast, Ajani, the Greathearted, Archangel Elspeth, Oko and The Wandering Emperor. Proliferate adds loyalty every turn.
- **Cantrips that proliferate:** Contentious Plan, Experimental Augury, Tezzeret's Gambit, Atomize and Mutational Advantage.
- **Protection:** Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Swiftfoot Boots and the new counterspells.
- **Interaction:** Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Vindicate, Anguished Unmaking, Beast Within and Cyclonic Rift.

**Mana.** The deck has 34 lands and about 10 ramp or mana-rock cards. Colour sources are W 17.5, U 19.5, B 17.5 and G 19.5, measured before the Forest/Island cut; the cut only touched G and U.
- The check tool still suggests about 38 lands for this curve, and warns that W and B sit at 17.5 sources where Elspeth and Yawgmoth want about 27. That is a real limit of a four-colour deck, and the ramp that fetches basics partly makes up for it. If you find you stumble on lands, put the Forest and Island back.
- The simulation had some flaws. Atraxa was in the library rather than the command zone, so the numbers are slightly pessimistic. Its figures were:
  - mulligan rate 9.2%
  - all four colours available by turn 4 in about 78% of games
  - a proliferate engine piece cast by turn 4 in 33.8% of games
- The land-drop and "screw" figures (46.3% of games with all four land drops by turn 4) are an opening-turns model only. It ignores ramp, fetches and cantrips, so don't read them as the deck's real mana.

**Adjusting for matchups.** Commander has no sideboard, so these are swaps for the 99 between games.
- **Fast combo:** keep Force of Will and Fierce Guardianship, and hold Cyclonic Rift for the combo turn. Cut Sword of Truth and Justice or Norn's Choirmaster for a cheap counterspell like Counterspell or Mana Drain. Both are legal, though I haven't tested them.
- **Wrath or bounce decks:** don't overextend. Keep Teferi's Protection and Heroic Intervention up, lean on planeswalkers, and consider adding Eternal Witness. I checked that it is legal but haven't tested it here.
- **Counter-hate such as Solemnity, or opposing Vorinclex halving:** use Beast Within, Vindicate and Anguished Unmaking on it. Cankerbloom and Boseiju also kill enchantments or artifacts.
- **Slow creature decks:** these are the best matchups. A lifelinking flier plus Swords or Path keeps you ahead.

**Unverified.** Nothing here is tested against real opposing decks, and no Commander tournament data was available. The matchup claims are judgment. The land count is below the tool's recommendation, as noted above.

results.text:
I resubmitted the deck as a revised brew: Zurgo Bellstriker is the commander, and the deck is mono-red burn-aggro. The simulation on the revised mana shows 10.1% mulligans.

**Plan.** Zurgo is a one-mana commander that can dash back to hand, so the command zone stays castable all game. Cheap haste creatures and about 20 burn spells (Bolt, Chain Lightning, Burst Lightning, Fireblast and others) push damage. Laelia is the one engine piece. She is in the 99, not the command zone, because the engine lock required her in the main deck and the tool rejected a Laelia commander. The impulse spells exile cards from your library, which grows her. The fast hasty creatures are what the deck is built around.

**What I changed** (shell and mana only; the engine is untouched):
- **Lands:** 37 → 35, with 30 Mountains. The original 37 lands were too many for an average mana value of 2.28 and 22 one-drops.
- **Added:** Abrade and Embereth Shieldbreaker.
- **Cut:** two Mountains. I also removed one more spell to keep the deck at 100.
- **Why the artifact removal:** the top meta deck, Cloud, Midgar Mercenary (11.3% share), runs Skullclamp, Umezawa's Jitte, Sword of Fire and Ice, Portable Hole and Pre-War Formalwear in 100% of its lists. Abrade also kills small creatures.

**Mana and numbers.** Every land makes red. The tool flags the list as light (it recommends about 39 lands for a generic deck at this curve), and I kept 35 anyway. That is a judgment call for an aggro deck.
- I simulated a close version of the deck (Zurgo in the 99, no Laelia) with 30 Mountains and the same 35 lands.
- Mulligan rate was 10.1%.
- An average of 3.23 lands were in play on turn 4.
- A cheap threat (Zurgo, Goblin Guide, Swiftspear, Dragon's Rage Channeler or Emberheart Challenger) was castable by turn 3 in 38.0% of games. That figure counts only those five creatures, not the rest of the deck.
- The simulator doesn't model card abilities, so it doesn't tell you how often Laelia grows.

**Matchups** (judgment from the archetype lists, not simulated):
- **Worst: Cloud / white weenie.** Mother of Runes, Giver of Runes, Swords to Plowshares, Solitude and Drannith Magistrate all beat a single big threat. Play many small threats, burn the protection creatures first, and hold Laelia until a removal spell is spent.
- **Brigid green ramp:** the mana dorks die to Forked Bolt and Pyrokinesis. Go fast before Solitude, Swords and Parallax Wave stabilise them.
- **Winter, a slow black-green deck:** this should be your best matchup. Punish its slow start, then finish with burn.

**Sideboarding.** Duel Commander has no sideboard, so I submitted none. Adjust through your mulligans and your targets.

**Unverified.**
- Matchup claims are judgment.
- The thesis says "40 life", but I did not check the life total. Count lethal against your table's starting life.
- The deck leans heavily on one-for-one trades and has little card advantage beyond Laelia and the impulse spells.

results.prompt: Something weird but competitive for Premodern.
results.text:
**Deck: Mono-Blue Donate Control (brew, borrowing the Island base and counterspell suite from Stiflenought)**

**Plan.** Counter and cantrip your way to the late game. Cast Illusions of Grandeur (gain 20 life), then Donate it to the opponent. Bounce it with Chain of Vapor, Boomerang or Capsize, or wait for them to fail the cumulative upkeep. They lose 20 life. Morphling is a backup win condition.

**Changes from the submitted list.** I kept the engine as submitted (Illusions, Donate, bounce spells, Intuition, Merchant Scroll, Cunning Wish).
- **Lands:** 17 Islands became 20.
- **Cuts to make room:** one Mana Leak, one Deep Analysis and one Morphling.
- **Sideboard:** Brain Freeze became Stifle.

**Why the extra lands.** The simulation (5,000 games) with 17 Islands showed a 37.5% screw rate and 30.3% of games hitting land drops through turn 4. With 19 Islands, screw was 29% and land drops 38.9%. With 20, screw was 25.7% and land drops 44%. Flood stayed at 0.3%. The deck has mana sinks: Illusions' upkeep, Capsize buyback, Gush and Daze (both return Islands).

`check_deck` still flags 20 lands as high compared with Stiflenought's 17.1, and recommends about 24 for this curve. I'm trusting the simulation here, but it doesn't model cantrips.

**Combo speed.** The simulation says all three pieces (Illusions, Donate and a bounce spell) are in hand by turn 5 in only 8.9% of games. At least one of them is in hand in 23.5% of games. It reports no color problems (mono-blue). This is a control deck that wins late, not a turn-5 combo deck.

**Mana sequencing (my judgment).** Illusions on turn 4 means paying 2 for upkeep on turn 5, and that leaves 3 mana for Donate. The bounce then comes on turn 6, or the opponent fails their own upkeep first. Hold a counterspell for their answer in the meantime.

**Matchups.** These are judgment, not measured. Meta shares come from `meta`.
- **Sligh (9.9%) and Goblins (4.4%):** The 20 life gained from Illusions absorbs burn, and Counterspell and Mana Leak stop the early plays. Bring in 3 Hydroblast and 2 Blue Elemental Blast. Powder Keg is good against small creatures.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%):** This is a counterspell mirror, and they have Stifle, Daze and Foil. Bring in 3 Annul (it counters Phyrexian Dreadnought, an artifact) and Misdirection and Thwart. Hydroblast and Blue Elemental Blast are dead cards here.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%):** This is probably the hardest matchup, because Armageddon beats our 4-mana Illusions. My earlier note that Armageddon "breaks the upkeep" had it backwards. If Illusions is already donated, the opponent can't pay its upkeep after Armageddon and loses 20 life. Bring in 2 Back to Basics, which hurts their nonbasic lands (Gemstone Mine, Treetop Village, Windswept Heath, Rishadan Port, Wasteland) and does nothing to our Islands. Keep Counterspell, Mana Leak and Daze for Armageddon and Mongoose. Tormod's Crypt is 107 of the 160 Terrageddon lists.
- **Enchantress (12.5%):** They have no early pressure, so counter their enchantment engine. Bring in 3 Annul and 2 Back to Basics (Brushland, Serra's Sanctum and Windswept Heath are in every list). One caution: Solitary Confinement gives them shroud, so Donate can't target them. Bounce it with Capsize or Boomerang. Take out Hydroblast and Blue Elemental Blast.
- **Hermit Druid (5.5%) and Replenish (4.8%):** Bring in Stifle against Hermit Druid's activated ability. Add Tormod's Crypt against graveyard plans. Hydroblast is also in 74 Replenish lists, so it can be dead cards for them too.

**Unverified or weak points.**
- Intuition is awkward here, because the opponent picks the worst of three cards. It is part of the locked engine, so I left it.
- Cunning Wish fetches only instants. That means the Hydroblasts, Annul, Stifle, Misdirection and Thwart.
- I haven't measured any matchup win rates, and the deck has no tournament results of its own. Illusions and Donate show 0 recent lists.
